problem:
Consider a function $z(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L\{z(t)\}=Z(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L\{{e}^{6t}z(t)\}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{{e}^{6t}z(t)\} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,z(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

2.Proving the First Shifting Theorem?

Consider a function z(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{z(t)}=Z(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{e6tz(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

est⋅e6tz(t)
e−st⋅e6tz(t)
e−st⋅e−6tz(t)
est⋅e6tz(t)
est⋅e−6tz(t)
e−(s−6)t
e−(s−6)t
e−(s+6)t
e(s−6)t
e(s+6)t
Z(s−6)
Z(s−6)
Z(s+6)
Z(s)
s>s0+6
s>s0+6
s>s0
s>s0−6
L{e6tz(t)}=∫0∞{(e−st⋅e6tz(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e−(s−6)t)(S1)}z(t)dt={(Z(s−6))(S2)}for{(s>s0+6)(S3)}.
